one_month_reasoning: The window contains Intel's Q3 2026 report (expected Thu 2026-10-22 after the close; date per earnings calendars, not yet confirmed). Guide was $15.8-16.8B revenue, 42% non-GAAP GM, $0.38 non-GAAP EPS vs consensus $0.39 / $16.43B. Channel trackers (BuySellRam, Fusion) show server CPU list prices up 10-20% since March with another 8-10% Xeon hike signaled for H2 and ~40% allocation fulfillment, and management said supply linearity was back-end loaded into late Q3/Q4, so a beat and a firm Q4 guide are more likely than not. But the stock rose 40%+ in September on narrative (Meta agent app, SK Hynix/Apple/Terafab reports) rather than new numbers, so a good print is largely expected and reversal risk after a sharp month offsets post-earnings drift. Net: I keep the median at ~$120 (P(>=120)=0.495, a hair under neutral for reversal risk) with a ~20% one-month log-sigma (76% annual / 3.5, with earnings in the window), roughly symmetric in log space.

fair_value.method: Blend of 50% forward P/E ($2.90 CY2028 EPS x 33x = $96) and 50% SOTP (Products $17.5B after-tax x 22x = $385B + foundry option ~$110B + Mobileye/Altera stakes ~$9B, net cash ~0, over 5.285B shares = ~$95). The $120 price embeds more foundry success than is yet evidenced by external revenue ($293M in Q2).

~25% growth on $2.30 as capacity adds (18A ramp, 14A ~6k wpm end-2027) and foundry losses narrow; below the $3.44 high estimate because foundry still loses ~$8B/yr (Ashton) and capex >$20B.

Premium to TSMC's ~23x 10-yr average and Nvidia ~28x (Fool) for supply-constrained growth plus foundry optionality; Ashton uses 22-25x for Products alone. 33x on consolidated EPS that is depressed by foundry losses.
Post-August $20B offering at $95 (210.5M + 31.6M option shares) per Ashton's count; Q2 diluted 5.1B.

inputs_detail.derivation: Ashton base $15B; I add ~15% for continued Xeon pricing/allocation tailwind, offset partly by Steam share loss to AMD (54.0% vs 58.6% a year earlier) in client.
Low end of Ashton's 22-25x range; near TSMC's 23x long-run average since CPU pricing is cyclical.

~50% chance of a firm high-volume 14A/18A-P commitment (Apple/others) by Oct-2027 worth ~$180B, else ~$40B (strategic/government-backed capacity). Haircut for SemiAnalysis-reported 14A slip to 2029 volume, dissenting 18A yield data (SemiWiki/Morgan Stanley 50%), and near-zero Ohio hiring (2 listings).

bear.story: CPU shortage eases as AMD/Arm capacity arrives and hyperscaler capex digests; Xeon price hikes reverse, margins slip back toward high-30s; no binding 14A volume customer by mid-2027 (SemiAnalysis-style schedule slips), Apple/Terafab stay 'preliminary'. Stock rerates to ~25x $2.50.

base.story: Supply-constrained CPU cycle persists through 2027, EPS ~$2.3 CY27 / $2.9 CY28; one or two 14A/18A-P commitments announced but small near-term revenue; multiple compresses from ~60x to ~40x CY28 as earnings catch up. Roughly flat.

bull.story: Apple M-series on 18A ships in 2027 and a large 14A anchor (Apple/Nvidia/Terafab) signs with prepayments; agentic-AI CPU demand keeps EPS revisions rising (CY28 >$3.5); market values foundry as a TSMC alternative.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$70 (about 25x my ~$2.8 standalone Products-based EPS with little foundry value, and 26% under the $95 August offering price) the market would be saying the CPU pricing/allocation cycle has broken or the foundry customer pipeline (Apple, 14A, Terafab) has failed. That is more than ordinary 76%-vol noise from a $120 base over a few months.

reasoning: Facts: $120 close, ~5.285B shares (~$634B cap), net cash ~0, Q2 non-GAAP EPS $0.42 on $16.1B (+25%), DCAI +59%, Q3 guide $0.38. Consensus EPS is $1.52 FY26 / $2.06 FY27, so the stock trades ~58x FY27, and FY27 consensus has risen ~35% in 90 days. My lane's evidence: (1) channel pricing trackers (BuySellRam, Fusion) confirm a real server-CPU shortage, with list prices up 10-20%, ~40% allocation fill and 30+ week lead times, supporting further upward revisions; (2) independent newsletters split: Ashton's SOTP says ~$250B of the cap is unproven foundry value and puts base value at $115-130; Intellionaire is very bullish; Semiecosystem/KeyBanc reports Apple 18A M-series for 2027; (3) social: KeyBanc-sourced customer lists (X) versus SemiAnalysis flagging a 14A slip; (4) alt data with negative tilt: Steam share falling to 54% Intel from 58.6%, Ohio job listings near zero (Ohio fab not ramping), Vanda showing retail-driven flows; (5) no open Intel prediction markets; resolved Q2 Polymarket brackets matched reported figures. Valuation: P/E ($96) and SOTP ($95) blend to ~$95, below spot, because current EPS growth supports roughly $90-100 and the rest depends on foundry wins that remain unsigned. Distribution: I centre the 12-month median at ~$112 (between fair value and spot; momentum and revisions argue against a full move to fair value) with log-sigma ~0.6 (below the trailing 76% realized vol, which included a regime change, but well above a typical large-cap's 25-35%). I fatten the lower tail slightly for a cycle reversal. Scenario mean is ~$119 (28% at $65, 47% at $115, 25% at $190), consistent with P(>=120) of about 0.46. Research limits: Reddit and X blocked direct fetching, so social content came via search snippets and is treated as leads; factual claims used in numbers (pricing, customers) have second sources.
